analysis_trace: Trial NCT06134050 is a randomized controlled trial comparing two correction targets (55% vs 62% of tibial width) in opening wedge high tibial osteotomy (HTO) using patient-specific instrumentation (PSI). The primary endpoint is KOOS Quality of Life (QOL) subscore at 24 months. Secondary endpoints include KOOS-12, FJS-12, EQ-5D, UCLA activity score, and ground contact time via accelerometer.

Evidence retrieved: (1) PMC9891955 meta-analysis confirms PSI improves HTO accuracy with no significant difference between planned and achieved correction for HKA and mMPTA. (2) PMC8808800 reports median KOOS QOL of 59.4 (MAD 21.9) at mean 3.1 years post-HTO, with pain 76.4, symptoms 75.0, ADL 85.3, sports 50.0. (3) PMC9977790 identifies age and preoperative WBL% as factors influencing outcomes. (4) PMC4901793 describes the Fujisawa point at 62% tibial width as traditional target.

Evidence-role assessment: PMC8808800 provides indirect_direction for KOOS outcomes (similar procedure, different population, no PSI comparison). PMC9891955 provides mechanism_background on PSI accuracy. No direct evidence compares 55% vs 62% correction targets specifically. No retrieved evidence provides numeric estimates for KOOS-12, FJS-12, EQ-5D, UCLA, or ground contact time at 24 months post-HTO with PSI.

Population matching: Retrieved studies include similar populations (medial compartment OA, varus deformity, age range overlapping with trial's 30-60 years). However, none use the specific 55% vs 62% comparison or 3D-printed PSI as in this trial.

Prediction rationale: Based on HTO literature, both correction targets (55% and 62%) are within acceptable ranges for valgus correction. The 62% target (Fujisawa point) is historically established, while 55% represents a more conservative correction. Given PSI accuracy demonstrated in meta-analysis, both groups expected to achieve planned correction with satisfactory clinical outcomes. KOOS QOL typically improves post-HTO but rarely reaches population norms. Predicted mean KOOS QOL at 24 months: 60-70 points for both groups, with non-inferiority likely demonstrated. KOOS-12, FJS-12, EQ-5D expected to show similar patterns of improvement. UCLA activity score typically improves to 6-8 range. Ground contact time lacks sufficient evidence for precise prediction.

Uncertainty: High uncertainty due to absence of direct comparative evidence for 55% vs 62% targets, lack of specific PSI outcome data at 24 months, and no published results from this specific trial. Confidence limited by reliance on indirect evidence from conventional HTO studies.

Safety considerations: HTO with PSI has demonstrated safety in meta-analysis. Risks include nonunion, infection, over/under-correction. Triple-blinding reduces detection bias for patient-reported outcomes.
